In [[mathematics]], and especially [[complex geometry]], the '''Mabuchi functional''' or '''K-energy functional''' is a [[Functional_(mathematics)|functional]] on the space of [[Kähler potential]]s of a compact [[Kähler manifold]] whose [[critical point (mathematics)|critical point]]s are [[constant scalar curvature Kähler metric]]s. The Mabuchi functional was introduced by [[Toshiki Mabuchi]] in 1985 as a functional which integrates the [[Futaki invariant]], which is an obstruction to the existence of a [[Kähler–Einstein metric]] on a Fano manifold.<ref>Mabuchi, T., 1985. A functional integrating Futaki's invariant. Proceedings of the Japan Academy, Series A, Mathematical Sciences, 61(4), pp. 119–120.</ref>

The Mabuchi functional is an analogy of the log-norm functional of the [[moment map]] in [[geometric invariant theory]] and [[symplectic reduction]].<ref>Thomas, R.P., 2005. Notes on GIT and symplectic reduction for bundles and varieties. Surveys in Differential Geometry, 10(1), pp. 221–273.</ref> The Mabuchi functional appears in the theory of [[K-stability]] as an analytical functional which characterises the existence of constant scalar curvature Kähler metrics. The slope at infinity of the Mabuchi functional along any [[geodesic]] ray in the space of Kähler potentials is given by the [[Donaldson–Futaki invariant]] of a corresponding [[test configuration]].

Due to the variational techniques of Berman–Boucksom–Jonsson<ref>Zhang, K., 2021. A quantization proof of the uniform Yau-Tian-Donaldson conjecture. ''arXiv preprint arXiv:2102.02438''.</ref> in the study of Kähler–Einstein metrics on Fano varieties, the Mabuchi functional and various generalisations of it have become critically important in the study of [[K-stability of Fano varieties]], particularly in settings with singularities.

== Definition ==

The Mabuchi functional is defined on the space of Kähler potentials inside a fixed Kähler [[cohomology class]] on a compact [[complex manifold]].<ref name="Szekelyhidi">Székelyhidi, G., 2014. An Introduction to Extremal Kahler Metrics (Vol. 152). American Mathematical Soc.</ref> Let <math>(M,\omega)</math> be a compact Kähler manifold with a fixed Kähler metric <math>\omega</math>. Then by the [[ddbar lemma|<math>\partial \bar \partial</math>-lemma]], any other Kähler metric in the class <math>[\omega]\in H^2_{\text{dR}}(M)</math> in [[de Rham cohomology]] may be related to <math>\omega</math> by a smooth function <math>\varphi\in C^{\infty}(X)</math>, the Kähler potential:

:<math>\omega_\varphi = \omega + i \partial \bar \partial \varphi.</math>

In order to ensure this new two-form is a Kähler metric, it must be a [[positive form]]:

:<math>\omega_\varphi > 0.</math>

These two conditions define the space of '''Kähler potentials'''

:<math>\mathcal{K} = \{ \varphi: M \to \mathbb{R} \mid \varphi\in C^{\infty}(X),\quad \omega + i \partial \bar \partial \varphi > 0\}.</math>

Since any two Kähler potentials which differ by a constant function define the same Kähler metric, the space of Kähler metrics in the class <math>[\omega]</math> can be identified with <math>\mathcal{K}/\mathbb{R}</math>, the Kähler potentials modulo the constant functions. One can instead restrict to those Kähler potentials which normalise so that their integral over <math>M</math> vanishes.

The tangent space to <math>\mathcal{K}</math> can be identified with the space of smooth real-valued functions on <math>M</math>. Let <math>S_\varphi</math> denote the [[scalar curvature]] of the [[Riemannian metric]] corresponding to <math>\omega_\varphi</math>, and let <math>\hat S</math> denote the average of this scalar curvature over <math>M</math>, which does not depend on the choice of <math>\varphi</math> by [[Generalized Stokes theorem|Stokes theorem]]. Define a differential [[one-form]] on the space of Kähler potentials by

:<math>\alpha_\varphi (\psi) = \int_M \psi (\hat S - S_\varphi) \omega_\varphi^n.</math>

This one-form is closed.<ref name="Szekelyhidi" /> Since <math>\mathcal{K}</math> is a [[contractible space]], this one-form is [[exact differential form|exact]], and there exists a functional <math>\mathcal{M}: \mathcal{K} \to \mathbb{R}</math> normalised so that <math>\mathcal{M}(0)=0</math> such that <math>d\mathcal{M} = \alpha</math>, the '''Mabuchi functional''' or '''K-energy'''.

The Mabuchi functional has an explicit description given by integrating the one-form <math>\alpha</math> along a path. Let <math>\varphi_0</math> be a fixed Kähler potential, which may be taken as <math>\varphi_0=0</math>, and let <math>\varphi_1=\varphi</math>, and <math>\varphi_t</math> be a path in <math>\mathcal{K}</math> from <math>\varphi_0</math> to <math>\varphi_1</math>. Then 

:<math>\mathcal{M}(\varphi) = \int_0^1 \int_M \dot \varphi_t (\hat S - S_{\varphi_t}) \omega_{\varphi_t}^n dt.</math>

This integral can be shown to be independent of the choice of path <math>\varphi_t</math>.

== Constant scalar curvature Kähler metrics ==

From the definition of the Mabuchi functional in terms of the one-form <math>\alpha</math>, it can be seen that for a Kähler potential <math>\varphi\in \mathcal{K}</math>, the variation 

:<math>\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=0} \mathcal{M}(\varphi + t \psi) = \int_M \psi (\hat S - S_\varphi) \omega_\varphi^n</math>

vanishes for all tangent vectors <math>\psi \in C^{\infty}(M)</math> if and only if <math>\hat S = S_\varphi</math>. That is, the critical points of the Mabuchi functional are precisely the Kähler potentials which have constant scalar curvature.<ref name="Szekelyhidi" />
